title: Apple's new Mac mini and Mac Studio with M6 and M5 Ultra chips optimized for local AI development
summary: Apple has announced updated versions of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, featuring new M6 and M5 Ultra chips designed to enhance local AI inference and software development. The M6 is Apple's first 2nm chip, offering improved CPU and GPU performance, while the M5 Ultra provides massive memory capacity (up to 512GB) and bandwidth (1.2TB/s), catering to AI workloads. These updates leverage the unified memory architecture and Thunderbolt 5 for distributed AI inference, making them popular among developers and researchers running large language models locally. The devices also include standard upgrades like Wi-Fi 7, faster storage, and improved Ethernet options.
key_points: Apple introduces the M6 (2nm) and M5 Ultra chips, optimized for local AI inference and software development.
M6 features a 12-core CPU (2 super cores, 4 performance cores, 6 efficiency cores) and a 12-core GPU, with up to 40% faster multi-threaded performance than the M4.
M5 Ultra combines two M6 Max chips, offering 36 CPU cores, 80 GPU cores, and up to 512GB of unified memory with 1.2TB/s bandwidth.
Mac mini and Mac Studio support distributed AI inference via Thunderbolt 5 and MLX, an open-source framework for machine learning on M-series chips.
Devices include Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, faster storage (15GB/s), and upgraded Ethernet (2.5Gb standard, 10Gb optional).
Pricing starts at $899 for the Mac mini (M6) and $2,499 for the Mac Studio (M5 Max), with higher-end configurations available.
Shipments begin September 22, with macOS 27 Golden Gate pre-installed.
